small_guidance:
- The current kernel parallelizes only over (N*OC)=2048 programs, which under-occupies the 4090. Add an output-tile dimension: split the pooled spatial grid (PD*PH*PW=1500) across programs via a 2D grid `(N*OC, ceil(total_pooled/BLOCK_P))` and atomic-add partial sums into the (N,OC) output, eliminating the serial outer loop.
- Expand autotune to include BLOCK_P in {8, 16, 32} (with the new 2D grid the per-program work is smaller) and add num_warps=1 configs; also key the autotuner on MK so the inner static loops specialize.
- Cache the per-(oc) weight slab (IC*KD*KH*KW=432 floats) in registers/shared once per program instead of re-issuing `tl.load(w_ptr + w_off)` inside the BLOCK_P loop — weights are reused for every pooled position.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a scatter-add ConvTranspose3d producing the full (N,OC,OD,OH,OW) tensor in channels_last layout, fused with `*scale`, then a second small kernel does maxpool+global-avg+clamp. The current gather formulation forces redundant work because each output voxel re-reads all IC weights; a scatter from (N, IC, ID*IH*IW) using the (IC,OC,KD,KH,KW) outer product reuses each input value KD*KH*KW*OC times.
- Alternatively, implement im2col-style GEMM: treat ConvTranspose3d as `weight^T @ input` followed by col2im scatter-add. Tile over (OC, output-spatial) with BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=IC*KD*KH*KW=81 — small enough to fit one K-tile, enabling a single `tl.dot`.
- Fuse maxpool + global-avg + clamp into the epilogue of the conv kernel by writing only the pooled+reduced output: each program owns one (n, oc) and a tile of pooled positions, accumulates a running sum (no atomic if one program per (n,oc) handles all pooled tiles via persistent loop, or with atomics if split). Critically, restructure the inner loops so the IC reduction is the innermost contiguous dim and the (kd,kh,kw) loop is outer — current code has IC innermost but only 3 channels, wasting the vectorization opportunity. Loop over pooled-tile in the inner axis instead so the BLOCK_P vector dimension drives memory throughput.
